text:
alex-cust: Hey team — our CI started failing on prod deploys after a key rotation last night. We see 401s from the Redwood API: 

ops-bot: [deploy-prod] 2026-03-14T23:12:03Z — ERROR — Upload failed: 401 Unauthorized: token_revoked

alex-cust: Timeline: we rotated our GitHub secret (REDWOOD_DEPLOY_KEY) around 22:50 UTC to a new long-lived key. After that, every GH Actions job that calls /v1/deploys returns 401. Rolling back the secret to the previous key fixes it immediately. We need a safe rotation strategy that doesn't cause downtime.

maria: Sorry about the disruption — can you paste the minimal deploy step and the error snippet (full request id if available)? Also which Redwood account/org and service account was used to mint the key?

alex-cust: Org: acme-inc. We used the service account named ci-deploy-bot. Request id from the logs: req_0b3f9a12. Deploy step (redacted):

```
name: Deploy
uses: actions/checkout@v3
env:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_DEPLOY_KEY }}
run: |
  curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deploys" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"service":"web","tag":"$GITHUB_SHA"}'
```

jason: Thanks. Two quick hypotheses: 1) The new key was issued with different scopes (missing deploy:write); 2) The key was created as a long-lived personal token vs an ephemeral SA-scoped token and the platform blocked it due to rotation policy / reuse detection.

kevin: I'm looking up req_0b3f9a12 — found the API request and the auth failure: 

```
{"time":"2026-03-14T23:12:03Z","req_id":"req_0b3f9a12","status":401,"error":"token_revoked","meta":{"sa":"ci-deploy-bot","token_id":"tk_9ff3d"}}
```

kevin: Token tk_9ff3d was created 2026-03-14T22:50:02Z and then shows a revoke event at 2026-03-14T22:51:10Z by user ajones (manual rotation). That explains the immediate 401s when the GH runner tried to use the token after it had been revoked.

maria: Ok — that fits. Two things: we should document a zero-downtime rotation flow, and we should check least-privilege of ci-deploy-bot. For short term recovery, you rolled the secret back which worked. For a clean rotation: create a second token, add it to GH secret, wait for jobs to pick it up, then revoke the old token.

alex-cust: That's what we did but we took the old token out too early while some runners were still using cached agents. Any tips to avoid that race?

jason: Yes — recommended pattern: use token overlap window + ephemeral tokens OR use OIDC/short-lived tokens so you avoid secret flips. Options in order of safety: 
1) Ephemeral token approach (recommended): issue short TTL tokens to runners at job start using an exchange step. Example using redwoodctl (or the API):

```
# create ephemeral token for SA with 1h TTL
redwoodctl tokens create --sa ci-deploy-bot --scopes "deploy:write,services:read" --ttl 1h --label gh-action-run
# prints token -> export to env and run deploy
```

This prevents long-lived secret rotation issues and limits blast radius.

2) Overlap window: create new long-lived token, add to GH secrets as REDWOOD_DEPLOY_KEY_NEW, update workflow to try NEW then fallback to OLD for a fixed window, e.g.:

```
REDWOOD_KEY=${{ secrets.REDWOOD_DEPLOY_KEY_NEW }} || REDWOOD_KEY=${{ secrets.REDWOOD_DEPLOY_KEY }}
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" ...
```

Use a controlled rollout: set window to > maximum runner lifetime (eg 2h). After window, revoke OLD.

3) Use Redwood's GitHub integration for deploys (recommended for orgs): connect via app so tokens are managed by the platform and rotate automatically.

kevin: Also checked the service account scopes. ci-deploy-bot had broad scopes: ["*"]. Strongly recommend narrowing to just what deploy needs: deploy:write, images:read, logs:read. We'll create a scoped policy and show commands.

maria: Alex — do you want us to create a scoped token for you and walk through an OIDC flow example? We can also patch your GH workflow to request ephemeral tokens while we do the change.

alex-cust: Yes please — that'd be great. Minimal disruption is key (can't have deploys blocked for >30m). If you can provision the token and give us steps we can update the pipeline during low-traffic window.

jason: Plan: 1) Create new SA-scoped token with limited scopes and 1d TTL (safety overlap). 2) Push token to GH as REDWOOD_DEPLOY_KEY_TEMP. 3) Patch workflow to try REDWOOD_DEPLOY_KEY_TEMP first; keep old secret intact. 4) Monitor for 1 hour. 5) Switch to ephemeral tokens via OIDC in a follow-up.

kevin: I'll create the scoped token and audit logs now. Commands I'm running:

```
# create service-account-scoped token (console or via CLI)
redwoodctl iam policy create --name ci-deploy-min --rules '[{"resource":"deploys","verbs":["create"]},{"resource":"services","verbs":["read"]}]'
redwoodctl iam service-accounts update ci-deploy-bot --add-policies ci-deploy-min
redwoodctl tokens create --sa ci-deploy-bot --scopes "deploy:write,services:read" --ttl 24h --label rotation-2026-03-14
```

ops-bot: Token tk_a4c7e created for sa=ci-deploy-bot label=rotation-2026-03-14 ttl=24h

kevin: I've sent tk_a4c7e to you via the SCIM-protected channel (do not paste here). Add it to GH secrets as REDWOOD_DEPLOY_KEY_TEMP.

maria: After you add it to GH, update workflow to try the TEMP key first (we'll provide a small wrapper script). Example wrapper to reduce racy flips: 

```
# try-temp-then-old.sh
if [ -n "$REDWOOD_DEPLOY_KEY_TEMP" ]; then
  KEY=$REDWOOD_DEPLOY_KEY_TEMP
else
  KEY=$REDWOOD_DEPLOY_KEY
fi
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deploys -d ...
```

alex-cust: Added the secret, patched the action to test in staging first. Staging deploy passed with temp token. Pushing to prod window in 10 minutes.

maria: Nice. After prod passes we should schedule a short follow-up to convert to OIDC. I can include step-by-step docs for GitHub Actions + redwoodctl exchange.

jason: One more note: avoid granting wildcard scopes to service accounts. We will run a project-wide scan and flag SAs with "*" scope and reach out to owners.

alex-cust: Thanks everyone. Two quick asks: 1) can you add a short doc snippet we can keep in our repo about rotation best practices? 2) can you make sure the audit log shows who rotated the token (to help us root-cause internal ops)?

maria: Yes to both. I'll paste a one-paragraph best-practices blurb here and attach the audit link: 

- Rotation best practices: avoid flipping long-lived secrets directly (use overlap windows or ephemeral tokens). Prefer OIDC / short TTL tokens for CI. Scope service accounts with least privilege. Always set a TTL and automate rotations.

maria: Audit link for your org: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/acme-inc/audit?filter=token_rotations&since=2026-03-14 — shows ajones revoked tk_9ff3d at 22:51 UTC.

kevin: I'll open a tracking ticket to run the org-wide SA scope audit and notify owners. Ticket RD-INC-2026-547.

alex-cust: Prod deploy succeeded during the window. All good now. Appreciate the quick help. :thumbsup: 

maria: Great — following up with the OIDC migration docs and a small patch we can PR into your repo. Leaving this thread open until OIDC is in place.

jason: If anyone wants, we can run a 15-min session to walk through the GH Actions OIDC exchange end-to-end.

alex-cust: Please, that would be helpful. Thanks again!
